Theme 071 · Data storytelling

Nightingale Rose

Florence Nightingale's 1858 polar-area diagram as a film grammar: an engraved, sepia-paper rose where every wedge is a slice of time and its length is the value. Pulse turns an hour of checkouts into a full teal flower; the anomaly is the three wedges since 09:42 that fall short of the dotted norm.

readability ●●○trust ●●●effort med
1 · HOOK0:00–0:08

Sepia wedges grow outward from the centre clockwise, one hour per 16th note, like a clock hand painting; the busy daytime petals bloom last and the italic today lands on the downbeat.

2 · REVEAL0:08 (drop)

On the drop all petals snap to equal length and re-colour teal in one clockwise sweep; the centre disc opens and the Acme mark rotates in 30° on beat 2.

3 · PROOF MOMENT0:12–0:32

The hour rose paints clockwise from :00; at 09:42 the wedges come in short and coral against a dashed norm on the snare, the leader line draws to −18% and the decision strip slides in.

4 · CTA0:36–0:45

A small even teal rose spins a quarter turn and settles; Every minute lands on the downbeat, then Start free presses on the final bar.

COMPONENT KIT

  • Rose wedge — polar-area slice, radius = value, paper gutters between petals
  • Scale rings — dashed concentric circles so length is readable
  • Norm ghost — dashed wedge outline showing the expected value
  • Clock labels — mono :00 / :15 / :30 or hour ticks around the rim
  • Engraved title — letter-spaced serif caps with a hairline rule, 1850s atlas style
  • Leader + note — ink elbow line to a serif marginal note

MOTION · MUSIC

  • Clockwise bloom — wedge radius 0 → value with power2.out 0.3 s, staggered 0.125 s (16ths at 120 BPM) around the dial
  • Petal equalise — all radii tween to one length with expo.inOut 0.5 s landing on the drop; hue sweeps clockwise over 1 beat
  • Short wedge — anomaly wedges stop 20 % short with back.in(1.2) 0.25 s on the snare; dashed norm draws around them

WHY / RISK · ADAPT IT

The rose is one of the most famous persuasive charts ever made — it was designed to make decision-makers act, which is exactly the Pulse story. Risk: radial charts are harder to compare precisely; always show the dashed norm.

Adapt to your product: Any cyclical metric (hours of a day, days of a week, minutes of an hour) works as a rose; swap in your own cycle and show the anomaly as wedges that fall short of their dashed expected shape.

References: datavizcatalogue.com/methods/nightingale_rose_chart.html (polar area / coxcomb chart definition and Nightingale's 1858 diagram)
